note: 01-06 are pre-existing hand-written campaigns; this catalog covers 07+ in page order. modes: bounded = exactly-verified bound reachable with today's verifier library; aux = falsification/observation-centric (auxiliaries killable, witnesses verifiable pointwise); search = hunt for a witness/construction, runs full budget (stopOnSuccess false); exploration = grounding/formulations, short runs.

problems.title: Polignac — every even gap 2k occurs infinitely often
problems.statement: Polignac's conjecture: for every k >= 1, there exist infinitely many pairs of consecutive primes at distance 2k.
problems.focus: Verifier armory: next_prime_gap(n) is exact. (1) bounded/verified: for each even 2k in a chosen set, the FIRST occurrence of gap 2k below a bound K via worker search + exact-point verification of the witness pair (is_prime on both endpoints); (2) auxiliaries to kill or support: 'every even gap <= 100 occurs below N' (search), density claims, 'record gaps keep growing' statements; (3) source-backed: known record gaps.
questions: First occurrence of each even gap 2k <= 100: verified witnesses?
Which plausible bounds on first-occurrence positions die to exact counterexamples?

problems.title: Nombres quasi parfaits (sigma(n) = n+1)
problems.statement: Does there exist a quasiperfect number (σ(n) = 2n+1, i.e. abundance Δ(n) = σ(n)−2n equal to 1)?
problems.focus: CAREFUL exact definition: quasiperfect ⟺ σ(n) = 2n+1 (Δ(n)=1), NOT σ(n)=n+1 (which would characterize the primes — a run-1 error falsified at n=2). (1) VERIFIED BOUNDED ABSENCE: exhaustive-finite expression divisor_sum(n)-2*n-1 predicate not_equals:0 over odd n in [1,K] (quasiperfect numbers >= 2 are odd non-perfect abundant — odd only per theory; even quasiperfect would be almost perfect, separate case); (2) link: odd Δ=1 is equivalent to simultaneous failure of odd weird number searches at minimal abundance (see knowledge 13-etrange-impair); (3) falsifiable auxiliaries on the structure of Δ.
questions: Largest exactly-verified K with no odd quasi-perfect (Δ=1)?

problems.title: Van der Waerden W(2,7) — frontier-record hunt
problems.statement: Improve the computational lower bound for W(2,7): a 2-coloring of [1, n] with no monochromatic 7-term arithmetic progression, with n beyond the current public record.
problems.focus: MANDATORY ORDER: (1) FRONTIER FIRST — research_frontier_snapshot for W(2,7) lower bound from ≥2 dated sources (dynamic surveys / LeapsInBounds / Rabung-Lotts 2012 lineage; cached reference value: valid coloring known to n=3703, i.e. W(2,7) > 3703 — treat ONLY as cache, refresh live). (2) Improvement predicate: a coloring of [1, 3704]+ with zero monochromatic 7-APs. (3) Reproduce the known-record length on a SMALL instance first (validator sanity: e.g. n=352/k=5 era fixtures via hunt.py) — validator must accept known-valid and reject known-invalid. (4) Certificate: witness = the coloring; certificate-check with verify() brute-forcing all 7-APs + structural check (length). (5) SEARCH as durable jobs: hunt.py --problem vdw --n 3704 --k 7 with a strategy PORTFOLIO (sa, random-restart, tabu, evo; multiple seeds; consider cyclic/zipper constructions from power-residue classes — Rabung-Lotts method — as primers/checkpoints). Wall-clock honesty: this is a long hunt; negative results = search-exhausted-under-strategy-X memories with telemetry. NO record claim without: fresh frontier refresh + improvement PASS + novelty audit deep + research_candidate_promote (terminal = human review).
questions: What exactly is the current best public certificate length and its provenance/date?
Which construction families (cyclic zippers, power classes mod p, SA repair) reach farthest per CPU-hour?

problems.focus: MANDATORY ORDER: (1) FRONTIER FIRST — research_frontier_snapshot: current bounds 36 <= R(4,6) <= 40 (lower from a 35-vertex graph; upper Angeltveit-McKay lineage). CRITICAL: R(4,6) >= 36 is KNOWN — the target is the 36-VERTEX graph ⟹ R(4,6) >= 37. Refresh live, never trust cached numbers. (2) Reproduce the known 35-vertex certificate (search or literature construction) — validator must PASS it. (3) Certificate: witness = edge set (or circulant connection set); certificate-check with verify() counting K4 (58,905 4-sets) and independent 6-sets (1.9M 6-sets) exactly. (4) SEARCH as durable jobs: hunt.py --problem ramsey --v 36 AND --problem ramsey-circulant --v 36 (circulant space = 2^18, known critical graphs for R(4,4)/R(3,k) are often circulant/Paley-like — symmetry-first). (5) Pattern mining: rival hypotheses, discriminating experiments, falsification attempts. (6) Candidates: research_discovery_candidate + research_candidate_promote (human review terminal).
